NASB.1: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, 'My daughter, shall I not seek security for you, that it may be well with you?
NASB.2: 'Now is not Boaz our kinsman, with whose maids you were? Behold, he winnows barley at the threshing floor tonight.
NASB.3: 'Wash yourself therefore, and anoint yourself and put on your [best] clothes, and go down to the threshing floor; [but] do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
NASB.4: 'It shall be when he lies down, that you shall notice the place where he lies, and you shall go and uncover his feet and lie down; then he will tell you what you shall do.'
NASB.5: She said to her, 'All that you say I will do.'
NASB.6: So she went down to the threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.
NASB.7: When Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain; and she came secretly, and uncovered his feet and lay down.
NASB.8: It happened in the middle of the night that the man was startled and bent forward; and behold, a woman was lying at his feet.
NASB.9: He said, 'Who are you?' And she answered, 'I am Ruth your maid. So spread your covering over your maid, for you are a close relative.'
NASB.10: Then he said, 'May you be blessed of the LORD, my daughter. You have shown your last kindness to be better than the first by not going after young men, whether poor or rich.
NASB.11: 'Now, my daughter, do not fear. I will do for you whatever you ask, for all my people in the city know that you are a woman of excellence.
NASB.12: 'Now it is true I am a close relative; however, there is a relative closer than I.
NASB.13: 'Remain this night, and when morning comes, if he will redeem you, good; let him redeem you. But if he does not wish to redeem you, then I will redeem you, as the LORD lives. Lie down until morning.'
NASB.14: So she lay at his feet until morning and rose before one could recognize another; and he said, 'Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor.'
NASB.15: Again he said, 'Give me the cloak that is on you and hold it.' So she held it, and he measured six [measures] of barley and laid [it] on her. Then she went into the city.
NASB.16: When she came to her mother-in-law, she said, 'How did it go, my daughter?' And she told her all that the man had done for her.
NASB.17: She said, 'These six [measures] of barley he gave to me, for he said, 'Do not go to your mother-in-law empty-handed.''
NASB.18: Then she said, 'Wait, my daughter, until you know how the matter turns out; for the man will not rest until he has settled it today.'

ESV.1: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?
ESV.2: Is not Boaz our relative, with whose young women you were? See, he is winnowing barley tonight at the threshing floor.
ESV.3: Wash therefore and anoint yourself, and put on your cloak and go down to the threshing floor, but do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
ESV.4: But when he lies down, observe the place where he lies. Then go and uncover his feet and lie down, and he will tell you what to do.”
ESV.5: And she replied, “All that you say I will do.”
ESV.6: So she went down to the threshing floor and did just as her mother-in-law had commanded her.
ESV.7: And when Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then she came softly and uncovered his feet and lay down.
ESV.8: At midnight the man was startled and turned over, and behold, a woman lay at his feet!
ESV.9: He said, “Who are you?” And she answered, “I am Ruth, your servant. Spread your wings  over your servant, for you are a redeemer.”
ESV.10: And he said, “May you be blessed by the LORD, my daughter. You have made this last kindness greater than the first in that you have not gone after young men, whether poor or rich.
ESV.11: And now, my daughter, do not fear. I will do for you all that you ask, for all my fellow townsmen know that you are a worthy woman.
ESV.12: And now it is true that I am a redeemer. Yet there is a redeemer nearer than I.
ESV.13: Remain tonight, and in the morning, if he will redeem you, good; let him do it. But if he is not willing to redeem you, then, as the LORD lives, I will redeem you. Lie down until the morning.”
ESV.14: So she lay at his feet until the morning, but arose before one could recognize another. And he said, “Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor.”
ESV.15: And he said, “Bring the garment you are wearing and hold it out.” So she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and put it on her. Then she went into the city.
ESV.16: And when she came to her mother-in-law, she said, “How did you fare, my daughter?” Then she told her all that the man had done for her,
ESV.17: saying, “These six measures of barley he gave to me, for he said to me, ‘You must not go back empty-handed to your mother-in-law.’”
ESV.18: She replied, “Wait, my daughter, until you learn how the matter turns out, for the man will not rest but will settle the matter today.”

NLT.1: One day Naomi said to Ruth, “My daughter, it’s time that I found a permanent home for you, so that you will be provided for.
NLT.2: Boaz is a close relative of ours, and he’s been very kind by letting you gather grain with his young women. Tonight he will be winnowing barley at the threshing floor.
NLT.3: Now do as I tell you — take a bath and put on perfume and dress in your nicest clothes. Then go to the threshing floor, but don’t let Boaz see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
NLT.4: Be sure to notice where he lies down; then go and uncover his feet and lie down there. He will tell you what to do.”
NLT.5: “I will do everything you say,” Ruth replied.
NLT.6: So she went down to the threshing floor that night and followed the instructions of her mother-in-law.
NLT.7: After Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he lay down at the far end of the pile of grain and went to sleep. Then Ruth came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
NLT.8: Around midnight Boaz suddenly woke up and turned over. He was surprised to find a woman lying at his feet!
NLT.9: “Who are you?” he asked. “I am your servant Ruth,” she replied. “Spread the corner of your covering over me, for you are my family redeemer.”
NLT.10: “The LORD bless you, my daughter!” Boaz exclaimed. “You are showing even more family loyalty now than you did before, for you have not gone after a younger man, whether rich or poor.
NLT.11: Now don’t worry about a thing, my daughter. I will do what is necessary, for everyone in town knows you are a virtuous woman.
NLT.12: But while it’s true that I am one of your family redeemers, there is another man who is more closely related to you than I am.
NLT.13: Stay here tonight, and in the morning I will talk to him. If he is willing to redeem you, very well. Let him marry you. But if he is not willing, then as surely as the LORD lives, I will redeem you myself! Now lie down here until morning.”
NLT.14: So Ruth lay at Boaz’s feet until the morning, but she got up before it was light enough for people to recognize each other. For Boaz had said, “No one must know that a woman was here at the threshing floor.”
NLT.15: Then Boaz said to her, “Bring your cloak and spread it out.” He measured six scoops of barley into the cloak and placed it on her back. Then he returned to the town.
NLT.16: When Ruth went back to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, “What happened, my daughter?” Ruth told Naomi everything Boaz had done for her,
NLT.17: and she added, “He gave me these six scoops of barley and said, ‘Don’t go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
NLT.18: Then Naomi said to her, “Just be patient, my daughter, until we hear what happens. The man won’t rest until he has settled things today.”

AMP.1: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to Ruth, "My daughter, shall I not look for security and a home for you, so that it may be well with you?
AMP.2: Now Boaz, with whose maids you were [working], is he not our relative? See now, he is winnowing barley at the threshing floor tonight.
AMP.3: So wash and anoint yourself [with olive oil], then put on your [ best] clothes, and go down to the threshing floor; but stay out of the man's sight until he has finished eating and drinking.
AMP.4: When he lies down, notice the place where he is lying, and go and uncover his feet and lie down. Then he will tell you what to do."
AMP.5: Ruth answered her, "I will do everything that you say."
AMP.6: So she went down to the threshing floor and did just as her mother-in-law had told her.
AMP.7: When Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was happy, he went to lie down at the end of the stack of grain. Then Ruth came secretly, and uncovered his feet and lay down.
AMP.8: In the middle of the night the man was startled and he turned over, and found a woman lying at his feet.
AMP.9: So he said, "Who are you?" And she answered, "I am Ruth your maid. Spread the hem of your garment over me, for you are a close relative and redeemer."
AMP.10: Then he said, "May you be blessed by the LORD, my daughter. You have made your last kindness better than the first; for you have not gone after young men, whether poor or rich.
AMP.11: Now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do for you whatever you ask, since all my people in the city know that you are a woman of excellence.
AMP.12: It is true that I am your close relative and redeemer; however, there is a relative closer [to you] than I.
AMP.13: Spend the night [here], and in the morning if he will redeem you, fine; let him do it. But if he does not wish to redeem you, then, as the LORD lives, I will redeem you. Lie down until the morning."
AMP.14: So she lay at his feet until the morning, but got up before anyone could recognize another; Boaz said, " Do not let it be known that the woman came to the threshing floor [last night]."
AMP.15: He also said, "Give me the shawl you are wearing and hold it out." So Ruth held it and he measured out six measures of barley [into it] and placed it on her. And she went into the city.
AMP.16: When she came home, her mother-in-law said, "How did it go, my daughter?" And Ruth told her everything that the man had done for her.
AMP.17: She said, "He gave me these six measures of barley, and he said to me, 'Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.'"
AMP.18: Then Naomi said, "Sit and wait, my daughter, until you learn how this matter turns out; for the man will not rest until he has settled it today."

MSG.1: One day her mother-in-law Naomi said to Ruth, "My dear daughter, isn't it about time I arranged a good home for you so you can have a happy life?
MSG.2: And isn't Boaz our close relative, the one with whose young women you've been working? Maybe it's time to make our move. Tonight is the night of Boaz's barley harvest at the threshing floor.

MSG.6: She went down to the threshing floor and put her mother-in-law's plan into action.

MSG.8: In the middle of the night the man was suddenly startled and sat up. Surprise! This woman asleep at his feet!

NRSVCE.1: Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, “My daughter, I need to seek some security for you, so that it may be well with you.
NRSVCE.2: Now here is our kinsman Boaz, with whose young women you have been working. See, he is winnowing barley tonight at the threshing floor.
NRSVCE.3: Now wash and anoint yourself, and put on your best clothes and go down to the threshing floor; but do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
NRSVCE.4: When he lies down, observe the place where he lies; then, go and uncover his feet and lie down; and he will tell you what to do.”
NRSVCE.5: She said to her, “All that you tell me I will do.”
NRSVCE.6: So she went down to the threshing floor and did just as her mother-in-law had instructed her.
NRSVCE.7: When Boaz had eaten and drunk, and he was in a contented mood, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then she came stealthily and uncovered his feet, and lay down.
NRSVCE.8: At midnight the man was startled, and turned over, and there, lying at his feet, was a woman!
NRSVCE.9: He said, “Who are you?” And she answered, “I am Ruth, your servant; spread your cloak over your servant, for you are next-of-kin.”
NRSVCE.10: He said, “May you be blessed by the LORD, my daughter; this last instance of your loyalty is better than the first; you have not gone after young men, whether poor or rich.
NRSVCE.11: And now, my daughter, do not be afraid, I will do for you all that you ask, for all the assembly of my people know that you are a worthy woman.
NRSVCE.12: But now, though it is true that I am a near kinsman, there is another kinsman more closely related than I.
NRSVCE.13: Remain this night, and in the morning, if he will act as next-of-kin for you, good; let him do it. If he is not willing to act as next-of-kin for you, then, as the LORD lives, I will act as next-of-kin for you. Lie down until the morning.”
NRSVCE.14: So she lay at his feet until morning, but got up before one person could recognize another; for he said, “It must not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor.”
NRSVCE.15: Then he said, “Bring the cloak you are wearing and hold it out.” So she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley, and put it on her back; then he went into the city.
NRSVCE.16: She came to her mother-in-law, who said, “How did things go with you, my daughter?” Then she told her all that the man had done for her,
NRSVCE.17: saying, “He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, ‘Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
NRSVCE.18: She replied, “Wait, my daughter, until you learn how the matter turns out, for the man will not rest, but will settle the matter today.”

NET.1: At that time, Naomi, her mother-in-law, said to her, “My daughter, I must find a home for you so you will be secure.
NET.2: Now Boaz, with whose female servants you worked, is our close relative. Look, tonight he is winnowing barley at the threshing floor.
NET.3: So bathe yourself, rub on some perfumed oil, and get dressed up. Then go down to the threshing floor. But don’t let the man know you’re there until he finishes his meal.
NET.4: When he gets ready to go to sleep, take careful notice of the place where he lies down. Then go, uncover his legs, and lie down beside him. He will tell you what you should do.”
NET.5: Ruth replied to Naomi, “I will do everything you have told me to do.”
NET.6: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her to do.
NET.7: When Boaz had finished his meal and was feeling satisfied, he lay down to sleep at the far end of the grain heap. Then Ruth crept up quietly, uncovered his legs, and lay down beside him.
NET.8: In the middle of the night he was startled and turned over. Now he saw a woman lying beside him!
NET.9: He said, “Who are you?” She replied, “I am Ruth, your servant. Marry your servant, for you are a guardian of the family interests.”
NET.10: He said, “May you be rewarded by the LORD, my dear! This act of devotion is greater than what you did before. For you have not sought to marry one of the young men, whether rich or poor.
NET.11: Now, my dear, don’t worry! I intend to do for you everything you propose, for everyone in the village knows that you are a worthy woman.
NET.12: Now yes, it is true that I am a guardian, but there is another guardian who is a closer relative than I am.
NET.13: Remain here tonight. Then in the morning, if he agrees to marry you, fine, let him do so. But if he does not want to do so, I promise, as surely as the LORD lives, to marry you. Sleep here until morning.”
NET.14: So she slept beside him until morning. She woke up while it was still dark. Boaz thought, “No one must know that a woman visited the threshing floor.”
NET.15: Then he said, “Hold out the shawl you are wearing and grip it tightly.” As she held it tightly, he measured out about sixty pounds of barley into the shawl and put it on her shoulders. Then he went into town,
NET.16: and she returned to her mother-in-law. When Ruth returned to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, “How did things turn out for you, my daughter?” Ruth told her about all the man had done for her.
NET.17: She said, “He gave me these sixty pounds of barley, for he said to me, ‘Do not go to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
NET.18: Then Naomi said, “Stay put, my daughter, until you know how the matter turns out. For the man will not rest until he has taken care of the matter today.”

NIV.1:
Ruth and Boaz at the Threshing Floor
One day Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, “My daughter, should I not try to find a home for you, where you will be well provided for?
NIV.2: Is not Boaz, with whose servant girls you have been, a kinsman of ours? Tonight he will be winnowing barley on the threshing floor.
NIV.3: Wash and perfume yourself, and put on your best clothes. Then go down to the threshing floor, but don’t let him know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.
NIV.4: When he lies down, note the place where he is lying. Then go and uncover his feet and lie down. He will tell you what to do.”
NIV.5: “I will do whatever you say,” Ruth answered.
NIV.6: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law told her to do.
NIV.7: When Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he went over to lie down at the far end of the grain pile. Ruth approached quietly, uncovered his feet and lay down.
NIV.8: In the middle of the night something startled the man, and he turned and discovered a woman lying at his feet.
NIV.9:
“Who are you?” he asked.
“I am your servant Ruth,” she said. “Spread the corner of your garment over me, since you are a kinsman-redeemer.”
NIV.10: “The Lord bless you, my daughter,” he replied. “This kindness is greater than that which you showed earlier: You have not run after the younger men, whether rich or poor.
NIV.11: And now, my daughter, don’t be afraid. I will do for you all you ask. All my fellow townsmen know that you are a woman of noble character.
NIV.12: Although it is true that I am near of kin, there is a kinsman-redeemer nearer than I.
NIV.13: Stay here for the night, and in the morning if he wants to redeem, good; let him redeem. But if he is not willing, as surely as the Lord lives I will do it. Lie here until morning.”
NIV.14: So she lay at his feet until morning, but got up before anyone could be recognized; and he said, “Don’t let it be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.”
NIV.15: He also said, “Bring me the shawl you are wearing and hold it out.” When she did so, he poured into it six measures of barley and put it on her. Then he went back to town.
NIV.16:
When Ruth came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, “How did it go, my daughter?”
Then she told her everything Boaz had done for her
NIV.17: and added, “He gave me these six measures of barley, saying, ‘Don’t go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
NIV.18: Then Naomi said, “Wait, my daughter, until you find out what happens. For the man will not rest until the matter is settled today.”
